title: Introduce compact liveness manifest and release composer
author: Maya Rivers
description: Context: Onboarding churn for small/ephemeral model variants has been noisy for release notes and missed transient performance regressions. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a compact 'liveness manifest' (manifest.jsonl-lite) that captures per-model-profile liveness signals (last-seen, sampled-traffic-weight, occupancy-estimate, probe-score) and 2) a 'release composer' service that consumes manifests and selector diffs to generate concise delta release notes and a prioritized impact teaser for reviewers. Motivation: reduce manual signal-sifting during model rollouts, surface transient regressions caused by affinity/occupancy changes, and auto-compose contextual release blurb drafts to speed on-call and PM review. Work included (summary): - schema: add compact_liveness_manifest v1 (schema and serializer, size-optimized for S3/GC storage) - ingestion: lightweight agent that hooks into onboarding pipeline to emit manifest shards per-batch - composer: deterministic delta algorithm that compares previous and current manifests plus performance tokens to synthesize short release notes and a structured 'why this matters' line - CLI: new `rmd release-compose --from-manifest X --to-manifest Y --samples N` for local review and CI checks - hooks: GitHub action that attaches composed blurb to model-onboard PRs when linked_linear contains ENG onboarding keys - tests: unit tests for serializer/compat, e2e smoke using small sample workloads - docs: concise HOWTO and examples for product and SRE teams Checklist: [x] schema defined and validated [x] agent + serializer implemented [x] composer algorithm (+ deterministic ordering) [x] CLI and GH action wire-up [x] unit and smoke tests [x] docs and example blurb templates Changeset summary: commits (see commits field) and 8 changed files: schema, agent, composer service, cli, gh action, tests, docs, changelog glue. Impact and safety: composer produces non-destructive draft text and artifacts are stored under a review-only prefix by default. There is an opt-out tag `manifest:skip-compose` for sensitive manifests. Performance: manifest shard is intentionally compact (average 1.1 KB / profile); composer runs in ~350ms for 1k profiles (single CPU). Rollout plan: 1) merge behind feature flag; 2) enable in staging for 48h to collect sample manifests; 3) enable GH action for non-prod PRs; 4) after sign-off, flip feature flag for mainline. Related: ENG-1427 (onboard signal plumbing), ENG-1498 (release note automation).
